_readme: AI brain configuration. This file is hot-reloaded by bot.py once per second -- no restart needed.
All distances are Geometry Dash world units (1 block = 30 units), all velocities are units/second,
all accelerations are units/second^2. The physics block is expressed per-second on purpose so
the 240 Hz simulation in bot.py is framerate independent. Where it helps, the 60 fps equivalent
is written in _doc fields (multiply per-frame velocity by 60, per-frame gravity by 3600).
Keys starting with '_' are documentation only and are ignored by the bot.

network._doc: The C++ bridge sends a state packet every processCommands tick and replies are sent back to the sender address. plan_interval_ms is how often the beam search is allowed to run; between plans the previous plan is reused (anti-spam + low CPU). The mod setting 'udp-port' must match port.

visuals._doc: trajectory_step sends every Nth simulation point (4 keeps lines smooth while keeping packets small). send_risk adds a compact 0..100 danger value per path point so the C++ overlay can fade the neon line to yellow/red near obstacles. show_alt_paths/show_corridor only add data for the 'showcase'/'debug' presets.

profiles._doc: The C++ bridge overrides 'active' with the profile selected by F8 (style_profile in the packet). 'smooth' plays like a human, 'tryhard' is for tight demons.

smooth._doc: max_cps: hard cap on real button switches per second. min_switch_ticks: minimum hold/release duration (240 Hz ticks) unless the current hold dies within solver.emergency_horizon_ticks. click_penalty: score cost of every hold change inside the search. hysteresis_bonus: score bonus for the still-valid previous plan. safe_corridor_deadzone: width of the central corridor band where centering corrections earn nothing (kills wave/ship 'sawtooth'). macro_step_ticks: branching period.

tryhard._doc: Same fields as 'smooth' but tuned for precise wave/spam sections and very narrow corridors.

solver._doc: lookahead_ticks: horizon length (96 ticks = 0.4 s at 240 Hz; more at 2x-4x speed in world units). beam_width: surviving branches per macro step. adaptive_tight_threshold: corridor height (units) below which click_penalty is scaled down smoothly so razor-thin spam corridors stay passable. emergency_horizon_ticks: if keeping the current button state dies within this many ticks, min_switch_ticks/max_cps are ignored. time_budget_ms: soft CPU budget per plan (the search degrades gracefully when exceeded).

physics._speed_doc: base_speed is the 1x horizontal speed in GD units/second. Speed portals received as type codes 10..14 select the matching multiplier. If the measured horizontal speed (EMA over packets) is available the bot prefers it, so a slightly wrong base_speed does no harm.
physics._doc: Cube defaults match the classic GD values (jump = 11.180032 u/frame * 60, gravity = 0.876 u/frame^2 * 3600). Ship/wave/ball/robot/spider values are approximations meant to be calibrated in-game with the overlay on: tweak a number, watch the predicted line, save, repeat (config hot-reloads in ~1 s). player_hitbox is the lethal solid hitbox, hazard_hitbox the smaller spike hitbox GD actually uses.
